label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: The designer wrote a third note. Dev built the designer's first.
findings.why: A run of short sentences with unexplained names (dev, deck, ruv-sgit, wake) reads as a log, and a newcomer cannot tell who does what.

findings.quote: Hour seven opened with the night's failure coming round a third time.
findings.why: The narrator reports what the record shows in the third person of events, with no I and no hindsight about why it matters.

findings.quote: None of the values was a key, an account credential, a vault key or a personal detail.
findings.why: I have not been told what a vault key is or what was captured, so this sounds alarming and then is left unexplained.

findings.quote: Three rounds, one picture, and I started none of them.
findings.why: It restates the three rounds the paragraph and the figure have just shown, as a triad.

findings.quote: put a check into the gate that fails any text size off the scale
findings.why: Gate, type scale and check are used without explanation, and the paragraph packs two events into one block that I skim.

findings.quote: A piece marked ready for me, then another. A list of what waits on me, refreshed every hour.
findings.why: Fragments stacked on one another where one sentence could carry the thought of the queue piling up.

findings.quote: Nine hours. Every wake started by the clock. Every wake with its five stages.
findings.why: The closing recap tells the whole chapter a second time in clipped sentences, and I would rather be told what it means for me.

findings.quote: the temptation is to start asking straight away
findings.why: It assigns me a temptation, and the card never says what I should actually read or do, which is the step I was looking for.

findings.quote: This is this book's conductor, not the talk's, and this book's storyteller and researcher too
findings.why: Two teams, two conductors and two storytellers in one sentence is where a reader with no background loses the thread; a plain one-line orientation is needed before this scene.

findings.quote: who it was, where its files are, what it was in the middle of, and the first things to do
findings.why: The handover's contents are listed here and then walked through again heading by heading under the next section.

findings.quote: a new session makes and publishes its own ... and never copies a private half across.
findings.why: Key, public key and private half arrive with no word on what the key is for, so the point of the line is lost on someone new.

findings.quote: Hey, I'm the librarian. The index of the source.
findings.why: Twelve near-identical self-introductions in a row is a wall I would skim, and I could not tell which two or three matter for starting out.

findings.quote: An early draft of the 30-page edition's chapter 1
findings.why: Editions and draft numbering are not explained, so the first failure begins with a reference I cannot place.

findings.quote: when it merged dev's work, the page that came out was dev's, word for word
findings.why: The third failure depends on merges, parents and commit order, which a non-coder cannot follow in one long paragraph.

findings.quote: rebuilding it from its parts and its record will show you what the record was missing
findings.why: Good idea, but for someone with one finished app it does not say what the parts or the record would be.

what_holds: 09-nine-hours-with-nobody-starting-work.md: the partial wake that says so, and the empty queue with the maker waiting on the editor, make the idea of an unattended team feel real and checkable.
20-sessions-end.md: the distinction between a member and a session, and the handover read out section by section, is something I could copy tomorrow for my own project.
21-the-second-factory.md: 'You do not need all of these to start' answers my question directly, and the failures kept in at full size build trust.
notes: As a first-build finisher I wanted the next step I can take; chapter 20 gives it (a handover and a debrief), chapters 9 and 21 mostly show the team's insides. Words used before explained: wake, gate, session (explained in 20 only), debrief, vault key, factory (after ch 2 presumably).
